title: The layers pulled onto one palette
question: Is B closer to what you meant by a shared colour palette -- one rock in several shades, rather than six different rocks?
context_md:
You said it twice, on two different cards: *'the color changes between layers is too much. There is too much contrast. There should be more of a shared color palette.'* This is that. Same seed, same ground, same binary -- only the rock colours moved.

Each bed is pulled two thirds of the way onto one shared warm-grey hue, and its brightness spread is squeezed by a fifth. **The brightness difference is what is left doing the work**, deliberately: the file's own history records that squeezing the *brightness* made the banding disappear from the picture entirely, so that is the one axis I did not touch much.

The six rocks are unchanged as materials -- they still differ in strength, which is what the new relief is built on. This is only their tone.

**Not addressed here, and I want to know if it still bothers you:** the sandy yellow patches now stand out more than they did, because everything around them got quieter. And the layers still run right up to the ground surface -- you asked for them to start deeper, which is next.
